raw_response:
I'm 78 years old. I've farmed these same 3 mu in Quzhou for 55 years, and me and my old lady know every furrow. The extension fellow keeps saying we should put down 18 kg of nitrogen per mu for the wheat, but I tried that back in 2019 and the wheat got too tall and lodged flat in that June windstorm. I learned my lesson. I usually do about 15 kg per mu total for wheat, split between base and topdressing, and a bit less for maize. Fertilizer prices are still high this year, so I'm not going to experiment.

For wheat, I'll plow under the maize stubble in early October, spread about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before sowing, and plant around October 12th. Come spring, if the wheat looks yellow at jointing, I'll topdress another 15 kg of urea per mu. I'll irrigate twice — once when it greens up in late March, and again at heading if it's dry. The well water isn't free anymore, they meter it now, so two times is my limit.

For summer maize, right after we cut the wheat in early June, I'll plant hybrid seed. Tight window, so no time for fancy tillage. I'll put down about 40 kg of compound per mu at planting, and if July is dry, I'll irrigate once, maybe twice. I don't hire labor — it's just me and my wife. We move slower now, but 3 mu is still manageable if we pace ourselves and don't try to rush.

I expect about 380 kg per mu for wheat and maybe 420 kg per mu for maize if the weather holds. Total costs need to stay around 1,600 yuan, or we'll be digging into our savings for medicine and food.
